body:
Update on the dependency I flagged above: Nutroot Transactions, #445 no longer needs this.

A Nutroot change quote's id is now derived from its lock key, `hex(tagged_hash("Cashu_QuoteId", pubkey))` (cashubtc/nuts@5923036). A wallet that lost its state can derive its NUT-13 `0x04` keys by counter and fetch the ids directly, stopping at a gap, the way NUT-13 restore works for proofs.

Floating it here because the same rule would settle the thread above.

If every locked quote took its id from its lock key, one key names one quote. There would be no max quotes per pubkey, no pagination, no new endpoint, and restore needs nothing but the seed. A reused locking key is simply refused.

Uniqueness comes from the quote id index mints already have. A later scheme that wants several quotes per key could salt the derivation without adding an index.

The cost: a wallet reusing one static key across many quotes would have to stop. NUT-13 wallets already don't. This PR would then be the compat path for mints that keep assigning their own ids.

Some overall comments, not really approving or disapproving of the idea or the implementation:

The PR description says "Golomb-Rice coded filter", while later it was rewritten for Bloom filters. It's good to clean this up thoroughly, so that a reviewer doesn't need to see these contradictions. The PR description should be up-to-date and concise

This implies that mint must keep all the bloom filters forever, even after all relevant keysets have expired. That seems too strict. When Cashu really takes off, this would be a huge dataset, and would be increasing quickly; I predict a lot of mints will simply disable this

> Uniqueness comes from the quote id index mints already have

A fair objection, voiced by me in previous discussions that led us to adopt UUIDv7: a derived id is a hash, so it inserts into the quote table at a random position, where a v7 id appends at the tail.

Random-keyed B-tree inserts cost more than appends, making UUIDv7 the natural choice over deterministic IDs. But that choice was made when locking was optional and lookup by pubkey had not been conceived.

Against this proposal it does not hold, for three reasons.

1. Mints already run far hotter random-keyed tables. Every swap inserts one `Y` per spent proof and one `B_` per issued output, both uniformly random by construction, and both tables grow with every operation. One quote row per quote, inserted once, is a rounding error beside them. If random inserts were a problem, Cashu would already have it.

2. The cost is paid on insert only. A lookup by id is a point read, O(log n) whether the key is time-ordered or hashed. The retrieval paths that matter, a wallet polling its quote or redeeming it, are unaffected.

3. The alternative is not "no random index". Lookup by pubkey, which this PR adds, is a secondary index on a 33-byte random key over the same table, maintained on every insert. So the comparison is one random index (derived id as the primary key) against two (time-ordered primary plus a random secondary). Deriving the id is the cheaper shape, and it has no result sets to bound.

Mints that want time-ordered storage can keep a v7 surrogate as the row key and index the derived id, which is exactly the secondary index they would need for the pubkey lookup anyway.

Update: the template leaf now carries a time. This limits the obligation on the mint to track issued change quote ids, as well as limiting the chances of permanent lockout on the leaf when outputs expire (eg keyset rotation).

This makes the covenant more like a "trust fund", the conditions apply until the time, then the parties are free to sign normally.

Vectors regenerated; cashu-ts#1290, nutshell#1198 and cdk#2654 updated to match.

Do you think that NUT-09 is the right place to put this:

_"define global sign-once behavior by canonical B_, regardless of amount or keyset"_

Maybe it should go somewhere else, like NUT00?

After agreement with @thesimplekid I pass here our short conversation on the topic:

>  Have you though about splicing at all? Thats kinda how I though liquidity management with mints between onchain and ln would work well. Though I know its not that well supported yet lnd not at all and not many cln and ldk mints out there. 
> 
> I think what you suggest in an interesting idea and I don't think would be too hard on the mint side. I think showing it to users would be harder though maybe most users would just not really notice this and only the special actors interested in doing the arbitrageur would have to worry about it. I think that is a potential down side as well as it needs these special actors but these days maybe thats just someones bot if the profit incentive is there.


> Thanks for pointing it out!
> 
> I see now that splicing can payout any onchain address - did not know that. So that might be indeed an additional option to weight against.
> Economically when splicing the costs are fully beared by the mint operator (as he is the one initiating it).
> 
> The question then is if we'd accept some added complexity to the protocol with aim to create a possible market incentives to mint ecash - and let some kid's bots doing the work. 
> 
> I still lean in favour of it, because it can compete in aggregate with splicing, normal transaction should be a little cheaper then 2 of 2 splicing one, and is really unique to how ecash works.

## Since 8 October

- Transcript: quote inputs (0x12) commit their lock key and `amount_issued`; blinded outputs (0x21) commit `SHA256(B_)`. Vectors regenerated.
- NUT-04: derived quote ids, `tagged_hash("Cashu_QuoteId", id_preimage)`; NUT-13 type 0x05 derives the preimage.
- NUT-22 request target is the path relative to the mint URL.
- Tighter malformed-input rules (witness entries, preimage length, spend info, NUT-13 scope and counter, NUT-28 slot index).

## Since 8 October

- Change quote ids derive from an `id_preimage` the wallet supplies, or, when it is omitted, from the transaction's inputs (new vector).
- With a melt, the melt quote is the transaction's record; the separate record and its route are gone.
- A pending input quote refuses other draws (20005).
- NUT-17 `change_mint_quote` kind.

## Since the 7 October review

- The template leaf names destination keys (`dests`) instead of hashing the outputs: every output must be a change quote to a listed key. Amounts and ids are the spender's.
- No time field; a timeout is an `after` leaf beside it.
- Vectors: covenant into two change quotes, and an arbiter escrow.

The one-shot discussion in [the earlier review](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/457#discussion_r4209544707) predates two changes: quote inputs now bind `amount_issued` (#443), so each signature authorizes one draw at one state of the quote, and with `dests` any later draw needs fresh signatures and can still only pay listed keys.
